pattern: Media platform: make uploads resumable and durable first, then process them asynchronously as a DAG of small retryable tasks; serve the bytes as cacheable adaptive-bitrate segments from a CDN so origin and API stay off the hot path; keep metadata cached, search in an event-fed index, and counters aggregated from a stream.

tips.nudge: Before anyone can watch, what does a creator do?
tips.hint: Write a functional requirement for getting a video into the system and published.
tips.show: F1/F2: Creators upload videos (resumable); uploads are transcoded into several resolutions and published.

tips.nudge: What do the other 800 million people do?
tips.hint: Write a functional requirement for playing a video on any device.
tips.show: F3: Viewers stream videos on any device and network; quality adapts to bandwidth.

tips.nudge: What do viewers notice first when a video platform is bad?
tips.hint: State targets for how fast playback starts and how often it stalls.
tips.show: N1: Playback starts in < 2 s and rarely rebuffers, worldwide.

tips.nudge: Which matters more: a video that can't play right now, or an upload that disappears?
tips.hint: Add non-functional requirements about availability and about losing uploads.
tips.show: N2/N3: Viewing 99.99% available; an uploaded original is never lost.

tips.nudge: Start from daily users and how many videos each one watches.
tips.hint: views/s = DAU × views per user / 86,400.

tips.nudge: How many streams are playing at once, and how many bits per second is each?
tips.hint: concurrent = views/day × average watch time / 86,400; egress = concurrent × average bitrate.
tips.show: egress = 27.8M concurrent × 3 Mbps ≈ 83,000 Gbps (≈ 80 Tbps).

tips.nudge: 500 hours arrive every minute. How much do you store for each hour of video?
tips.hint: storage/day = hours uploaded per day × bytes per video-hour across all renditions.
tips.show: storage_per_day = 720k h × ~3 GB ≈ 2,160 TB/day (~0.8 EB/year).

tips.nudge: A 20 GB upload on hotel Wi-Fi drops at 70%. What does the API let the client do?
tips.hint: A POST that starts an upload session, plus a way to send ranges and resume.
tips.show: POST /uploads {title, size} → {upload_id, upload_url}; PUT /uploads/{id} with Content-Range; resume from the last received byte.

tips.nudge: What does the player fetch to start playing, and from where?
tips.hint: A GET for the watch page metadata, and the manifest/segment URLs the player then pulls.
tips.show: GET /videos/{id} → {title, views, manifest_url}; the player GETs master.m3u8 and segments from the CDN.

tips.nudge: Between upload and playback a video goes through states. What do you store about it?
tips.hint: One record per video: identity, owner, descriptive fields, processing state and what renditions exist.
tips.show: videos(video_id, channel_id, title, tags, status, renditions[], manifest_url, duration) sharded by video_id.

checks.label: Processing uploads designed as its own part

tips.nudge: A 3-hour 4K upload must be watchable in many resolutions within minutes. How do you split the work?
tips.hint: Add a part for the pipeline: compare inline transcoding, one job per video and segment-level fan-out.
tips.show: Part 'Transcoding pipeline': resumable upload to object storage → DAG orchestrator splits into segments → segment × rendition tasks on a queue → stateless workers → package manifests → publish.

checks.label: Getting bytes to viewers designed as its own part

tips.nudge: ~80 Tbps, viewers from 2G phones to 4K TVs. Where do bytes come from, and in what shape?
tips.hint: Add a part for delivery: compare origin streaming, single-bitrate CDN and adaptive bitrate segments on a CDN.
tips.show: Part 'Delivery': HLS/DASH 2–6 s segments in a bitrate ladder, from CDN edges with an origin shield; the player switches rendition per segment.

checks.label: Metadata and search designed as their own part

tips.nudge: Watch pages need metadata at ~100k reads/s and users type queries. Same store for both?
tips.hint: Add a part for metadata and search: compare one SQL DB, a cached sharded DB plus a search index, and a single NoSQL store.
tips.show: Part 'Metadata and search': SQL sharded by video_id with a read-through cache; Elasticsearch fed by metadata-change events.

checks.label: View counting designed as its own part

tips.nudge: A viral video gets 20,000 views a second. What happens to its counter row?
tips.hint: Add a part for counting: compare incrementing per view, Redis INCR and aggregating events in windows.
tips.show: Part 'View counting': view events to Kafka by video_id; windowed workers dedupe and filter bots, then write batched increments.

tips.nudge: Can a few data centres push ~80 Tbps with a fast start in every country?
tips.hint: Put something between players and the origin that is near the viewer.
tips.show: A CDN with edges worldwide and an origin shield; segments and manifests are cached there.

tips.nudge: Who does ~300k cores' worth of work every day?
tips.hint: Add a fleet that processes uploads independently of the request path.
tips.show: Stateless transcode workers (ffmpeg) pulling segment × rendition tasks; preemptible capacity.

tips.nudge: Petabytes a year of immutable files. Database or something else?
tips.hint: Pick a store built for large immutable objects.
tips.show: Object storage for originals and for encoded segments/manifests (the CDN origin).

checks.label: Heavy processing decoupled from the upload request

tips.nudge: Should the upload request wait while the video is encoded?
tips.hint: Connect the upload/orchestration side to something asynchronous that workers consume.
tips.show: Orchestrator → encode task queue → transcode workers (the upload returns as soon as the original is stored).

tips.nudge: Which resolutions and codecs do you produce, and is it the same for every video?
tips.hint: Compare a fixed H.264 ladder with per-title ladders and newer codecs for some videos.
tips.show: Per-title ladder in H.264 for everything; VP9/AV1 only for videos past a popularity threshold, where the egress savings pay for the encode.

checks.label: Popular vs rarely watched content handled

tips.nudge: Most views go to few videos, most bytes stored belong to videos nobody watches. Does that change anything?
tips.hint: Think about caching, pre-warming and storage classes by popularity.
tips.show: Pre-warm the CDN for expected hits, origin shield for the long tail, move cold renditions to cheaper storage after ~90 days without views.

tips.nudge: What is the most expensive thing in this system, and what saturates first during an upload spike?
tips.hint: Walk the upload and playback paths and name what limits each.
tips.show: CDN egress and hit ratio; transcode capacity under spikes; hot metadata for viral videos; the orchestrator's state store.

tips.nudge: How would you know viewers in one country are buffering?
tips.hint: List player-side and pipeline-side metrics.
tips.show: Video start time and rebuffer ratio (player telemetry), CDN hit ratio per PoP, upload-to-publish latency, transcode queue depth, index and view-count lag.
